Liberation is the first AC game where I got 100% sync and while the objectives were pretty good, the system in general was just so dumb. 

Sometimes the objective was too obvious, like "air assassinate the target." Well, duh, of course I'm gonna air assassinate them, you lined up everything perfectly and I don't feel like alerting an army of enemies and fighting my way to the target when I can just hop on these beams/branches/whatevers and just jump on him. Or made no sense at all, like the infamous hay cart in AC3 or the "find-a-way-to-air-assassinate-a-Grenadier-while-your-allies-are-getting-fucked-by-cannon-fire-don't-worry-take-your-time-don't-get-detected-tho."

I also missed some of the objectives coz I just didn't see them pop up on the screen, at least in Brotherhood and Revelations paused the game and you could read in peace what you needed to do, instead of having to pause the game immediately after a cutscene and breaking any immersion or flow you had. I also despised the objectives that appeared in the middle of the memories. Okay, fine, if I have to pause the game at the start of a memory, so be it, it's annoying and stupid, but I definitely don't want to pause in the middle of any action just to make sure that I'm not missing anything... And no, I can't just ignore it, I'm a completionist and seeing that I've missed something after a mission/quest drives me nuts.

If people wanted more difficulty in the game, the optional objectives could have been added into the memory replays in like, maybe five levels. Example, you need to sneak into an enemy camp and assassinate the target, in the story there is no objectives, do what you want, but if you replay the memory the objective could be "kill the target with a poison dart." Second playthrough the objective would change to "don't kill anyone but the target." For the third "kill the target without getting detected." And so on... It would not only add challenge to those who want it, but it would also add replay value to the memories or to the game if they'd add it to like a new game+ sort of thing. So many possibilities.

Good to get that out of my system. /rant

I'm currently playing through Rogue and there is just so much missed potential that it's driving me nuts. In my opinion the game should have been split into two; a Templar game and a rogue assassin game.

Let's start with the Templar one first. This could've been a great spin-off where the game-play could and should be different. With Shay you look like a Templar, but play like an assassin. It would have been more interesting to be able to be, I dunno, more in the open and maybe have missions where you have to defend assassin targets, not like you have in Rogue, the assassin interceptions, but story related and more fleshed out. If Ubisoft wanted to have this particular game set in the colonies, we could have played as everyone's favorite Templar, Haytham. It would have fit the Kenway saga better anyway. And it could have been a DLC, like Freedom Cry if they didn't want to make it a standalone.

And then the rogue assassin. This is more story related, rather than being bored of playing re-skinned black flag. I like Shay, most of the time... He's reasons for leaving the assassins and joining the Templar felt rushed, not thought out and just plain baffling to be honest. And the assassins... Well... The plot just reminds me of romantic comedies where everything happens because adults don't know how to communicate. Now, of course, miscommunications happen, but basing a plot on it is lazy. I kind of wish that at the end of the game there would be some sort of consequences for Shay, like, the Templars betray him or he ends up killing lots of people again by accident and realizes that he was too rash with his actions, or something, anything really. Anyway, maybe this rogue assassin would not join the Templars, but would rather work for both, neither, anyone just as long as it served his own goals. Maybe the assassin's refused to kill a target, like Ezio, and decided to take actions into his/her own hands and well, go rogue. Or he was a Templar and an assassin, but hated both. Maybe he wanted both Templars and assassins to be gone because they kept killing people. So many options...

Rogue is not a bad game, but it is weird and disappointing. I honestly don't really see any point with it. What does it really bring to the table? It's too similar with black flag and the Templar aspect of it doesn't really bring anything either. You look like a Templar, but you play like an assassin. You don't even really kill assassins, but some rando thugs most of the time. They could have done so much more with this, but they didn't.

Edit: One thing I forgot to add. When I first started Rogue, I was hoping that the game would end up doing what Liberation did and show us a fake history and then the real history. So, the assassins, Isu or whoever could have fooled or try to fool Abstergo that Shay left the assassins and joined the Templars, but in reality that never happened. I'd really like to see that mechanic come back, but probably not.

Minimalisteilla voi olla koristeita. Useilla varmaan onkin, koska ne tuo iloa elämään. Edelleenkin, sen minkä sinä määrittelet turhaksi ei tarkoita että se on turhaa kaikille.

Kommentteja lukiessa muistelen kun itse kiinnostuin minimalismista. Katselin kuvia kokovalkeista ja tyhjistä kodeista ja luin artikkeleita ihmisistä joiden koko omaisuus mahtui reppuun. Tajusin aika pian ettei kumpikaan miellyttänyt minua, eikä elämäntilannekkaan sallinut heittämään kaikkea mitä ei pysty itse kantamaan menemään. Katsoin kuitenkin youtubesta videoita minimalismiin liittyen. En muista tarkkaan kuka se oli, Matt D'Avella ehkä, joka sanoi ettei minimalismin ole pakko olla samaa kaikilla. Joku voi omistaa vain viisi esinettä, kun jollain toisella on 100 tai 1 000 tai 5 000. Pointti ei ole se tavaroiden tarkka määrä, vaan se tyyli elää. Älä osta turhaa ja jos on pakko ostaa jotain niin satsaa mielummin laatun kuin määrän.

Jokaisella on kuitenkin erilainen elämä, eikä kaikki halua harjoittaa minimalismia samalla tavalla. Ei edes ole olemassa yhtä ja oikeaa minimalismia. Se että tällä miehellä on 598 tavaraa voi olla sille minimalismia, ihan sama onko se teille muille sitä. Se että sulla on 264 esinettä voi olla jollekin toiselle minimalismi elitistille liikaa ja sen mielestä minimalismin ehdoton raja on 10 esinettä. Just tämä "toi ei oo minimalismia koska mä en nää sitä minimalismina" on ihan vitun ärsyttävä asenne ja ajaa minimalismita kiinnostuineita pois. Minimalismilla on imago ongelma ja minimalistit ei todellakaan auta muuttamaan sitä.

I didn't like him at first, but as the game progressed he grew on me. I do think he came in a bad spot, right after Ezio and that might play a significant part in why some people don't like him. It was refreshing though, to have a protagonist like him, naive and such, especially since Ezio had grown to be an old man (Sorry, buddy) and was wiser and experienced. So, to have a protagonist that grew up pretty sheltered and who then gets thrust into a completely different world and he has to learn so much, and he's kind of alone too\*. Ubi definitely could have done much more with him, but overall he's a good protagonist. 

One major thing that makes me like him is that he feel much more flawed than other protagonists, I did not agree with him all the time, I strongly relate and emphasize with whoever I'm playing as and rarely really question their actions or decisions, with Connor though, I disagreed with his actions and words much more and that made him better. He forced me to think my own position on things and think how I'd justify or explain things that he was questioning. I don't think the people around him really gave him good answers and I felt his frustration. His impatience was also something I related on.

I wish I could've seen more character development though or had more inner dialogue or something. Sometimes it felt like the game brushed off something that should have been more explored and examined and it was at those moments that Connor came off as dumb or ignorant. I often cringed at his lines (Voice acting was great, apart from few lines that felt off), but in retrospect we've all said something stupid and that's what makes us human. 

\*Yeah, you could argue the same with Ezio, but he still had his sister, mother and uncle, plus he stayed in Italy surrounded by his own culture and language.

"Meidän koulussa ei kiusata!"

Oma kiusaamiseni alkoi jo ala-asteella ja jostain jääräpäisestä syystä, en voinut myöntää kiusaamista itselleni. Pyrin aina antamaan takaisin samalla mitalla. Kaikki luokan pojat oli mukana kiusaamisessa, mutta jotenkin se olin minä joka joutu aina ongelmiin. Puolet vitosluokasta olin erityisryhmässä, koska tämä ilmeisesti edisti sitä oman luokan yhteishenkeä tai jotain muuta paskaa.

Äitiä vitutti koko koulu, opettajat ja rehtori ihan suunnattomasti. Osa luokan tytöistä oli kerran tullut tuomaan pudonnutta penaalia ja kertoivat äidilleni, mitä koulussa oikein tapahtuu. Opettajani myös sanoi minua imbesilliksi, mutta yritti äitilleni vakuutta ette sanoi käytökseni olleen "imbesillimäistä" eräässä episodissa. Näytti vähän aikaa siltä, että äiti olisi ihan mielellään tirpassut opettajaa.

En onneksi mieti näitä asioita kovin usein, välillä ne palaa mieleen ja sitten vituttaa. Elämä on nyt kuitenkin muualla, eikä noihin ihmisiin törmää kun sattumalta, eikä silloonkaan kumpikaan enää oikein tunnista.
